entries.observed: Python project-local JSON and ECMAScript serialization differ for 1e-7; hashes differ.
entries.architecture_effect: Semantic/consensus hashes are deterministic only inside the current Python profile. Cross-language cryptographic identity is not established.
entries.required: Adopt and test a standards-conformant JCS implementation or define a different normative canonical format and cross-language vectors.

entries.observed: KXBD is a custom binary packet; no CBOR codec is used.
entries.architecture_effect: KEX binary boundary is project-specific and lacks standardized deterministic binary interchange.
entries.required: Either retain KXBD as explicitly private protocol with a formal spec/test vectors, or add deterministic CBOR profile and semantic binding.

entries.observed: Process and directory RPC use plaintext loopback TCP; no ssl/TLS layer is instantiated.
entries.architecture_effect: Loopback tests prove message mechanics but not authenticated/confidential/integrity-protected multi-host transport.
entries.required: TLS 1.3 transport profile plus peer identity verification, certificate/key lifecycle, replay/session policy and fault tests.

entries.observed: 13 observed databases pass integrity_check and use WAL + synchronous FULL.
entries.architecture_effect: Durable local journals are real, but SQLite WAL explicitly requires processes sharing a database to be on the same host.
entries.required: For multi-host deployment, each host needs local durable state plus replicated-log protocol; never place a shared WAL database on a network filesystem.

entries.observed: Layer-2 separates accepted desired state, observed manifestation, plan, effect, readback and NOOP convergence.
entries.architecture_effect: The reconciliation model now matches the desired/current control-loop discipline at a conceptual level.
entries.required: Production target-specific actuators/observers, retries, timeouts, compensation policy, status reporting and external-system qualification.

entries.observed: ToT voter and directory replica sets are fixed. Catch-up exists for known replicas; learner admission/promotion does not.
entries.architecture_effect: Rejoin of known identities is tested, but adding/removing voting members safely is unproven.
entries.required: Non-voting learner state, catch-up thresholds, explicit promotion, overlapping/joint configuration safety, removal fencing and persistent membership history.

entries.observed: Replica identity is a configured logical voter string, not a cryptographically attested workload identity.
entries.architecture_effect: Process identity, authorization and vote authenticity are not bound to a workload trust domain.
entries.required: Workload identity issuance/attestation, short-lived verifiable identities, trust bundle/key rotation and mTLS binding to vote/commit receipts.

entries.observed: Resident adapter casefolds lookup keys but does not apply Unicode normalization.
entries.architecture_effect: Canonical-equivalent Unicode spellings have not been proven to resolve to one semantic identity.
entries.required: Define NFC/NFKC policy per semantic domain, normalize before lookup/hash where intended, preserve original form for provenance, and add multilingual conformance vectors.

entries.current_comparison: VALID PRIVATE PROJECTION METADATA / NOT GENERIC SEMANTIC INTERCHANGE
entries.observed: HTML projection stores KEX/IL-LLM identity in data-* attributes.
entries.architecture_effect: This is suitable for application-private projection metadata, but WHATWG explicitly does not make data-* a generic cross-tool extension vocabulary.
entries.required: If public machine-interoperable semantics are required, define a stable external vocabulary/profile rather than treating data-* as universal authority.

entries.observed: R5 has terms, majority/quorum gates, committed prefixes, restart/catch-up and higher-term uncommitted conflict supersession. It still uses external ProcessCluster orchestration and fixed membership.
entries.architecture_effect: The mechanics are stronger than an in-process model but do not constitute Raft implementation/conformance.
entries.required: Autonomous peer timers/elections, replicated progress tracking, formally specified log conflict algorithm, membership changes, snapshots, proof/model checking and multi-host failure-domain tests.
